blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Biophilic Design

A Biophilic design, a movement related to green architecture, has gained much momentum within the building community in recent years. The premise of biophilic design is to avoid or minimise harmful impacts on the natural environment and, equally importantly, to provide and restore beneficial contacts between people and nature in the built environment.

B People have a psychologically developed need to commune with nature, but this has frequently been neglected. All too often, architects put creative originality before the needs of the people who must live and work in their futuristic constructions, with scant regard for emotional as well as practical considerations. Biophilic design does not advocate tree houses or cave-dwelling, but it does provide nature-based features that maximise human functioning and health. Though not technically a biophilic design, Fallingwater—the stunning house in rural Pennsylvania designed in the 1930s by Frank Lloyd Wright—arguably speaks to the human soul far more than the box-like blocks of flats designed by his contemporary Le Corbusier.

C In the modern world, much of our built environment obstructs the age-old connection between humans and nature. The rate of technological progress far exceeds the rate of psychological evolution, leaving us ill-equipped to cope with our lifestyles, which in turn leads to increased stress. Because biophilia attempts to integrate basic and current needs, it can alleviate the difficulties caused by the brain's constant efforts to function in a modern environment it has not yet evolved to handle. For example, one crucial element of the natural landscape for human health is sunlight. We are evolutionarily programmed to respond positively to sunny areas over dark or overcast ones and sense that they will foster restoration, improve emotional well-being and promote health.

D Because of its tremendous impact on human psychology, biophilic design plays a vital role in healthcare and its delivery. The current healthcare system contains many flaws, especially in its physical spaces. Hospitals, clinics and offices are high-stress environments for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals alike. One well-known study looked at the impact of nature on patients after surgery. One group had a view of a tree; the others had a window looking onto a brick wall. The first group had shorter hospital stays, received fewer negative comments from nurses, required fewer analgesics and had slightly fewer post-operative complications.

E As a consequence of this and other studies, nature and nature-based design have been integrated into the physical design of many hospitals. For example, Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center (DHMC) in New Hampshire boasts an atrium design illuminating the entire facility. Natural elements also permeate the building, including wood, stone and numerous live plants. While DHMC was built to incorporate these qualities, other hospitals have had biophilic features added to existing structures. The application of biophilic concepts to hospital interiors has increased substantially as administrators have witnessed patients' positive responses to nature.

F Many existing buildings contain biophilic elements, but only a few have been built with the specific idea of biophilic design in mind. One such building is the Adam Joseph Lewis Center for Environmental Studies at Oberlin College in Ohio. The director of Oberlin's Environmental Studies Program, David Orr, explained that the building's goals were “to create not just a place for classes but rather a building that would help to redefine the relationship between humankind and the environment—one that would expand our sense of ecological possibilities”. The Lewis Center is sustainable in a broader sense than in the typical application of the word. It harnesses solar power, utilises both active and passive air systems, and monitors the weather to adapt to conditions. The Centre's “Living Machine” treats wastewater by combining traditional wastewater technology with wetland ecosystems' purification processes, producing water that can be used in the toilets and for irrigation. In their design, Orr and his team of architects engineered a healthy and comfortable space for students while ensuring the surrounding environment was undamaged.

G Another example is the University of Guelph-Humber building in Ontario, Canada. It contains a centrally located bio-wall, vertically spanning the building. The wall is covered in dense foliage which not only connects people to nature on the inside of the building, but also functions as a new filtration-system prototype. The wall purifies the air and has the potential to fulfil the building's fresh-air-intake requirements. These examples prove that the built environment need not interfere with biological human needs to commune with nature, nor with existing ecological systems.

H Ancient architects built for their cultures, which were almost always more in touch with the earth than Western society is today. They mimicked nature's forms, producing magnificent structures that still awe us—though biophilic design is a novel concept, they certainly employed some of its recommendations. Today we can add another layer to this tradition and ensure maximal benefit for our planet and ourselves.

Questions 14–19

Reading Passage 2 has eight paragraphs, A–H.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–H, in boxes 14–19 on your answer sheet.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEFGH
14 a description of how rapid change has a negative effect on people
15 a reference to an architect whose designs were uncharacteristic of biophilia
16 a definition of the two main aims of biophilia
17 a positive claim about early forms of architecture
18 a reference to the fact that many architects are too focused on innovation
19 a description of features which conserve energy in a biophilic design

Questions 20–24

Complete the sentences below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

20 In the modern world, advancements are happening so quickly that humans are unable to adjust to them.

21 Biophilia can help us deal with the caused by the difficulties of our current lifestyles.

22 People instinctively feel more comfortable in places which have plenty of , something which is necessary for health and well-being.

23 An experiment designed to test the effect of nature on patient recovery times found that those who could see a made a faster recovery.

24 There is a biophilic design feature in the University of Guelph-Humber building which improves the quality of the .

Questions 25 and 26

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Which TWO of the following statements does the writer make about the Adam Joseph Lewis Center at Oberlin College?

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 亲自然设计（Biophilic Design）是绿色建筑相关运动，近年在建筑界迅速发展。其核心前提是 “避免或最小化对自然环境的有害影响”，且同等重要的是 “在人造环境中提供并恢复人与自然的有益联系”。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 人类在心理上有与自然交流的需求，但这一需求常被忽视。建筑师常将创意创新置于使用者需求之上，忽视情感与实用考量。亲自然设计不主张树屋或洞穴居住，而是通过自然元素最大化人类机能与健康。尽管弗兰克・劳埃德・赖特（Frank Lloyd Wright）1930 年代设计的宾夕法尼亚乡村 “流水别墅（Fallingwater）” 并非严格的亲自然设计，但其对人类精神的感染力，远胜于同时代勒・柯布西耶（Le Corbusier）设计的盒状公寓楼。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 现代人造环境阻碍了人类与自然的古老联系。技术进步速度远超心理进化速度，使人类难以适应现代生活方式，进而导致压力增加。亲自然设计试图整合人类基本需求与现代需求，缓解大脑在 “尚未进化适应的现代环境” 中运作的困境。例如，阳光是自然环境中对人类健康至关重要的元素 —— 人类进化出对阳光的积极反应（偏好阳光区域而非阴暗区域），认为阳光能促进恢复、改善情绪、有益健康。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 因对人类心理影响巨大，亲自然设计在医疗保健领域至关重要。当前医疗体系存在诸多缺陷，尤其在物理空间方面 —— 医院、诊所和办公室对患者、访客和医护人员而言均是高压力环境。一项知名研究观察自然对术后患者的影响：一组患者病房窗外有树，另一组面对砖墙。结果显示，看树的患者住院时间更短、护士负面评价更少、止痛药使用更少、术后并发症略少。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 受此类研究影响，许多医院将自然元素融入物理设计。例如，新罕布什尔州达特茅斯 - 希区柯克医疗中心（DHMC）采用中庭设计，照亮整个建筑，木材、石材和大量绿植等自然元素遍布建筑。DHMC 在建造时就融入这些元素，而其他医院则在现有建筑中添加亲自然特征。随着管理者见证患者对自然的积极反应，医院内部亲自然设计的应用大幅增加。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 许多现有建筑包含亲自然元素，但极少建筑在设计时明确以亲自然理念为核心，俄亥俄州奥伯林学院的亚当・约瑟夫・刘易斯环境研究中心（Adam Joseph Lewis Center）便是其中之一。奥伯林环境研究项目主任大卫・奥尔（David Orr）解释，该建筑的目标 “不仅是打造教学空间，更是重新定义人类与环境的关系 —— 拓展人类对生态可能性的认知”。刘易斯中心的可持续性远超该词常规含义：利用太阳能、采用主动与被动通风系统、根据天气调整运行模式；中心的 “活机器（Living Machine）” 将传统废水处理技术与湿地生态系统净化过程结合，处理后的水可用于冲厕和灌溉。奥尔及其建筑师团队在设计中，既为学生打造健康舒适的空间，又确保周边环境不受破坏。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 另一案例是加拿大安大略省的圭尔夫 - 亨伯大学（University of Guelph-Humber）建筑，中央有一面贯穿建筑的垂直生物墙（bio-wall），墙面覆盖茂密植被。这面墙不仅让室内人员接触自然，还作为新型空气过滤系统原型 —— 净化空气，有望满足建筑新风需求。这些案例证明，人造环境无需阻碍人类与自然交流的生理需求，也无需破坏现有生态系统。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph H
passageNotes.text: 古代建筑师为其文化而建，当时文化与自然的联系远比现代西方社会紧密。他们模仿自然形态，建造出至今仍令人惊叹的宏伟建筑 —— 尽管亲自然设计是新概念，但古人无疑采用了其中部分理念。如今，我们可在这一传统基础上进一步发展，确保人类与地球均能获得最大益处。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落匹配（Questions 14–19：Which paragraph contains the following information?）

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a description of how rapid change has a negative effect on people（描述快速变化对人类的负面影响）
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “The rate of technological progress far exceeds the rate of psychological evolution, leaving us ill-equipped to cope with our lifestyles, which in turn leads to increased stress”，明确描述 “技术进步过快导致人类适应困难、压力增加”，与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

（2）题目 15：a reference to an architect whose designs were uncharacteristic of biophilia（提及一位设计不符合亲自然理念的建筑师）
答案：B
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “Le Corbusier... box-like blocks of flats”，指出勒・柯布西耶设计的盒状公寓楼 “缺乏自然元素，不符合亲自然理念”，与题干对应，因此答案为 B。

（3）题目 16：a definition of the two main aims of biophilia（亲自然理念两大核心目标的定义）
答案：A
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “The premise of biophilic design is to avoid or minimise harmful impacts on the natural environment and, equally importantly, to provide and restore beneficial contacts between people and nature in the built environment”，明确定义 “两大目标：减少环境危害、恢复人与自然联系”，与题干对应，因此答案为 A。

（4）题目 17：a positive claim about early forms of architecture（对早期建筑的正面评价）
答案：H
解析：定位 Paragraph H 中 “Ancient architects... were almost always more in touch with the earth than Western society is today. They mimicked nature’s forms, producing magnificent structures that still awe us”，正面评价 “古代建筑与自然联系紧密、形态模仿自然、宏伟壮观”，与题干对应，因此答案为 H。

（5）题目 18：a reference to the fact that many architects are too focused on innovation（提及许多建筑师过度关注创新）
答案：B
解析：定位 Paragraph B 中 “All too often, architects put creative originality before the needs of the people who must live and work in their futuristic constructions”，“creative originality” 对应 “innovation”，指出建筑师 “将创新置于使用者需求之上”，与题干对应，因此答案为 B。

（6）题目 19：a description of features which conserve energy in a biophilic design（描述亲自然设计中的节能特征）
答案：F
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “It harnesses solar power, utilises both active and passive air systems, and monitors the weather to adapt to conditions”，描述 “利用太阳能、主动 / 被动通风、随天气调整” 等节能特征，与题干对应，因此答案为 F。

items.text:
（1）题目 20：In the modern world, \___\___\____ advancements are happening so quickly that humans are unable to adjust to them.
题目翻译：现代社会，\___\___\___\_进步速度过快，人类难以适应。
答案：technological（技术的）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “The rate of technological progress far exceeds the rate of psychological evolution, leaving us ill-equipped to cope”，“progress” 对应 “advancements”，明确提到 “技术进步过快”，因此答案为 “technological”。

（2）题目 21：Biophilia can help us deal with the \___\___\____ caused by the difficulties of our current lifestyles.
题目翻译：亲自然设计可帮助我们应对当前生活方式困境带来的_\___\___\___。
答案：stress（压力）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “which in turn leads to increased stress. Because biophilia attempts to integrate basic and current needs, it can alleviate the difficulties”，“alleviate the difficulties” 对应 “deal with”，明确提到亲自然设计缓解 “压力”，因此答案为 “stress”。

（3）题目 22：People instinctively feel more comfortable in places which have plenty of \___\___\___\_, something which is necessary for health and well-being.
题目翻译：人类本能地在_\___\___\___充足的地方感到更舒适，这对健康和幸福至关重要。
答案：sunlight（阳光）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “one crucial element of the natural landscape for human health is sunlight. We are evolutionarily programmed to respond positively to sunny areas”，明确提到 “阳光充足的地方让人舒适”，因此答案为 “sunlight”。

（4）题目 23：An experiment designed to test the effect of nature on patient recovery times found that those who could see a \___\___\____ made a faster recovery.
题目翻译：一项测试自然对患者康复时间影响的实验发现，能看到_\___\___\___的患者恢复更快。
答案：tree（树）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “One group had a view of a tree; the others had a window looking onto a brick wall. The first group had shorter hospital stays”，明确提到 “看树的患者恢复更快”，因此答案为 “tree”。

（5）题目 24：There is a biophilic design feature in the University of Guelph-Humber building which improves the quality of the \___\___\___\_.
题目翻译：圭尔夫 - 亨伯大学建筑中有一项亲自然设计特征，可改善_\___\___\___质量。
答案：air（空气）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “The wall purifies the air and has the potential to fulfil the building’s fresh-air-intake requirements”，明确提到 “生物墙净化空气，改善空气质量”，因此答案为 “air”。

题目：Which TWO of the following statements does the writer make about the Adam Joseph Lewis Center at Oberlin College?（关于奥伯林学院亚当・约瑟夫・刘易斯中心，作者提到以下哪两项？）
答案：B、D
选项 B：It is beneficial for both students and the environment.（对学生和环境均有益）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Orr and his team of architects engineered a healthy and comfortable space for students while ensuring the surrounding environment was undamaged”，明确提到 “为学生提供健康空间，且不破坏环境”，与 B 一致。
- 选项 D：It aims to inspire new ways of thinking about the environment.（旨在启发人们以新方式思考环境）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “the building’s goals were ‘to create not just a place for classes but rather a building that would help to redefine the relationship between humankind and the environment-one that would expand our sense of ecological possibilities’”，“redefine the relationship”“expand our sense” 对应 “inspire new ways of thinking”，与 D 一致。
- 排除 A：文中未提及 “首个亲自然教育建筑”；排除 C：文中未提及 “课堂设计新概念”；排除 E：文中仅提到 “利用太阳能”，未提及 “向周边建筑供电”。
